_meta.title: Megan Whitaker — Talkspace (postpartum anxiety)
_meta.why_strong: Single richest example. Time-anchored trigger (8 p.m. panic attack), competing alternatives compared on price ($200 house calls), spousal push, identity threat ('unfit psychotic mother'), and a strong post-purchase quote about the *mechanic* of why it worked ('typing in the middle of nursing').

persona.name: New-mom Megan, 32, postpartum anxiety + 1-month-old at home
persona.location_context: Suburban first-time mom, 1-month-old daughter recently hospitalized for breathing issues, husband works full-time outside the home, no nearby family
persona.primary_job: When I have a panic attack at 8pm while my husband holds the baby and I can't breathe, I want to talk to a real licensed therapist before midnight — without leaving my newborn in flu season or paying $200 for a house call I can't afford, so I can stop being someone whose anxiety runs the household.

pain_points.label: Acute panic attacks since hospital scare
pain_points.description: Daughter's 11-day NICU stay has triggered ongoing intrusive thoughts; first full panic attack happened at 8pm with hyperventilation, dizziness, racing heart

pain_points.label: Can't physically leave the house
pain_points.description: Nursing every 2 hours; flu-season exposure risk in waiting rooms; baby still on monitoring; can't drive 30 minutes to a therapist's office

pain_points.label: $200/session house-call therapist out of budget
pain_points.description: Researched in-home therapy; $200/session × weekly = unsustainable on one income while on maternity leave

pain_points.label: Identity threat: 'unfit mother'
pain_points.description: Terrified that seeking help will be filed somewhere as evidence she can't handle motherhood; hides the panic from her own mother and friends

trust_needs: Therapists are actually licensed (state-by-state) and credentials are visible
HIPAA compliance explicit — paranoid that anything goes on insurance EOB
Asynchronous text option so she doesn't need to schedule fixed time slots
Clear cancellation — terrified of being 'trapped' in subscription
decision_triggers: Husband sat her down after the panic attack and said 'this isn't normal, please get help'
Insurance not required (would have to deal with her insurance company otherwise)
Same-day or next-day match with a therapist
objections: Will this show up on my insurance EOB and freak my husband's HR out?
Are these therapists actually qualified for postpartum stuff?
If I cancel, will it be a fight?
persona.channel_behavior: Mobile only; nights between feeds; uses Reddit r/postpartumdepression for research; trusts other moms in community more than ads

verbatim_quotes: Typing out my concerns in the middle of nursing or during nap time became natural and truly therapeutic.
I just couldn't be the kind of mom who couldn't handle this.
I wasn't going to leave the baby in a waiting room during flu season.
